title: ～てある — a state left as a result of someone’s action
summary: Transitive verb て-form + ある describes a state that exists because someone did it on purpose: ‘has been done (and stays that way)’. The thing becomes the subject marked with が. It is often used to describe what you see in front of you.

patterns.form: ものが＋他動詞て形＋ある
patterns.gloss: thing + が + transitive verb te-form + ある (絵がかけてある)
place に + thing が + てある (壁に絵がかけてある)

body.p: Use a verb that takes an object (a transitive verb): かける, 置く, 貼る. Make the て-form and add ある. The thing, which was the object of the action, becomes the subject with が: 絵がかけてある.
It implies someone did this on purpose, and the result is still there. The person who did it is not mentioned. It is used to describe what you see: 机の上に花が置いてあります.
With an intransitive verb, ている shows a state (ドアが開いている, ‘the door is open’). With a transitive verb, てある shows a state someone made (ドアが開けてある, ‘the door has been opened (by someone)’).

examples.ja: 壁（かべ）に絵（え）がかけてあります。
examples.romaji: Kabe ni e ga kakete arimasu.
examples.tr: A picture has been hung on the wall.
examples.note: Someone hung it, and it is still there.

examples.ja: 机（つくえ）の上（うえ）に花（はな）が置（お）いてあります。
examples.romaji: Tsukue no ue ni hana ga oite arimasu.
examples.tr: A flower has been placed on the desk.
examples.note: 置く → 置いて + あります.

examples.ja: ドアに紙（かみ）が貼（は）ってあります。
examples.romaji: Doa ni kami ga hatte arimasu.
examples.tr: A paper has been put up on the door.
examples.note: 貼る → 貼って + あります.

pitfalls: Use a transitive verb and mark the thing with が: 絵がかけてある, not 絵をかけてある.
Don't use it with intransitive verbs like 開く; say ドアが開いている.
